patch_description: The best prior program (3401) used pure-greedy construction followed by an annealing insertion local search. The current program's ILS regressed (3247) likely because its limited insertion neighborhoods get stuck. Key parameters to tune: greedy exploration rate and sample count during construction. I implement a multi-restart construction where the greedy sample rate decays from 0.95 to 0.85 across restarts (`sample_rate = 0.95 - 0.10*(restart/max_restarts)`) and `num_samples` grows from 8 to 12, feeding each greedy solution into the proven annealing insertion descent. Early restarts exploit greedy signal; later restarts diversify. A cost cache avoids recomputation, and the best solution across restarts is returned within the time budget. This follows the recommendation (pure parameter mutation on the known-optimum region) while restoring the stronger local search structure.
